text:
ConocoPhillips fell 2.9% today as crude oil prices dropped sharply—US oil fell to $89.62 per barrel, down from the $140+ range the stock was trading at just days ago. While geopolitical tensions in the Middle East remain high (Iran attacks on Gulf installations, threats to shipping in the Strait of Hormuz), oil markets appear to be pricing in concerns that these conflicts won't actually disrupt supply flows significantly, or that demand weakness may outweigh supply-risk premiums.

The stock's decline over the past week mirrors the broader pullback in crude prices, which have given back recent gains despite genuine military escalation in the region. When oil traders lose confidence that geopolitical risk will translate into actual supply shortages, prices fall—and integrated oil companies like ConocoPhillips move with them.
